question: Should OpenClaw adopt `local`, `container`, `reverse-proxy`, and `node-mode` as the initial named, release-tested hosting support catalog over the separately proposed readiness facility?
rationale: The PR deliberately creates durable product, compatibility, and trusted-proxy support contracts; source review cannot determine whether those four postures and their long-term maintenance commitment match maintainer strategy.

options.title: Adopt the four-profile catalog
options.body: Accept the opt-in catalog and require the linked readiness and profile implementation work to prove unprofiled-upgrade compatibility plus each packaged posture before runtime landing.

options.title: Accept readiness without standard profiles
options.body: Keep RFC 0018 independent and defer named hosting contracts until maintainers choose a smaller or differently scoped support catalog.

options.title: Narrow the catalog before acceptance
options.body: Request that the RFC retain only the postures OpenClaw is prepared to release-test and support as stable contracts.

recommendation.title: Adopt the four-profile catalog
recommendation.body: Accept the opt-in catalog and require the linked readiness and profile implementation work to prove unprofiled-upgrade compatibility plus each packaged posture before runtime landing.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked readiness and hosting RFC stack and can clarify the intended boundaries, while the final product decision belongs with repository maintainers.
